I already know how to grow these two crops, the local weather fits them, and the selling market is clear. At the start of the season, I would keep the winter wheat that is already in the field, push for a stable grain yield with moderate fertilizer, a few irrigations, and only necessary pesticide sprays. After wheat harvest, I would sow summer maize right away so I do not lose time or soil moisture. I would use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I want stable yield and stronger stress resistance, but I would not make the plan too complicated. With my age, labor, and schooling, I would choose a simple, familiar, manageable system rather than trying too many crops at once.
